title: Autistic Girls: Misdiagnosis, Masking, and Breaking Stereotypes

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能赚到除了出卖时间换取金钱以外的收入，会怎样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士（Dr. Marianne Trent），自2019年以来，我一直在开发被动和经常性的收入来源。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有个好消息要告诉大家。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many program is now open for enrollment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特（Sophie Foote）的“一对多”（One-to-Many）项目现已开放报名。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我本人在2022年完成了该项目，此后也支持了两批心理学家走过他们的旅程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的联盟链接加入，你将获得苏菲的奖励，以及我提供的独家支持套餐，无需额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四场小组智囊团会议、大师班、个性化指导、一份福特纳姆和梅森（Fortnum and Mason）的礼品，以及限时的一对一辅导奖励。

sentences.en: Enrollment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于11月16日星期一晚上10点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过描述中链接的我的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时为你解答。

sentences.en: Why are so many autistic females overlooked, misdiagnosed, or diagnosed too late?
sentences.zh: 为什么这么多自闭症女性被忽视、误诊或诊断得太晚？

sentences.en: Today we are uncovering the hidden stories behind any statistics, exploring the unique ways autism presents in girls, and why traditional frameworks often fail them.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将揭开统计数据背后的隐藏故事，探索自闭症在女孩身上表现出的独特方式，以及为什么传统的框架往往无法帮助她们。

sentences.en: If you've ever wondered how masking, stereotypes, and societal expectations impact autistic girls, then stay tuned because this conversation is essential.
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经好奇过伪装、刻板印象和社会期望是如何影响自闭症女孩的，那么请继续收听，因为这次对话至关重要。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to the Aspiring Psychologist podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎来到《有抱负的心理学家》（Aspiring Psychologist）播客。

sentences.en: I am Dr. Marianne, and I'm a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安博士，我是一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: Now, today we are meeting someone who works as an assistant psychologist and who has a sister who is autistic herself and was diagnosed later than would have been ideal for her.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要见一位担任助理心理学家的嘉宾，她的妹妹也是自闭症患者，而且诊断时间比理想情况要晚。

sentences.en: Let's dive straight in, but please, if you do find this content helpful, please do like, please do comment.
sentences.zh: 让我们直接进入主题，但如果你觉得这些内容有帮助，请一定要点赞、评论。

sentences.en: It is the kindest thing you can do for any podcaster.
sentences.zh: 这是你能为任何播客主做的最贴心的事。

sentences.en: And please feel free to share the episode with people as well, perhaps with your colleagues, perhaps with your friends, perhaps with your family,
sentences.zh: 也请随意与他人分享这一集，也许是你的同事、朋友或家人，

sentences.en: whether that is a YouTube episode or the MP3 version too.
sentences.zh: 无论是YouTube视频版还是MP3音频版都可以。

sentences.en: I hope you find it so useful, and I will look forward to catching up with you on the other side.
sentences.zh: 希望你觉得它很有用，我期待在节目之后与你交流。

sentences.en: Hi, just want to welcome along our guest for today, Hannah, who is an assistant psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎我们今天的嘉宾，助理心理学家汉娜（Hannah）。

sentences.en: Hi, Hannah.
sentences.zh: 你好，汉娜。

sentences.en: Hi, Marianne.
sentences.zh: 你好，玛丽安。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: Oh, well, thank you for being here.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢你能来。

sentences.en: And thank you for pitching your episode to me as well.
sentences.zh: 也谢谢你向我推荐这一集。

sentences.en: So this is, of course, close to your heart, but you really wanted us to open up the narrative around autistic spectrum disorder diagnoses or autistic spectrum condition diagnoses,
sentences.zh: 这当然是你非常关心的话题，但你确实希望我们能拓宽关于自闭症谱系障碍或自闭症谱系状况诊断的叙述，

sentences.en: specifically in females and how that might look different for females compared to males.
sentences.zh: 特别是针对女性，以及这与男性相比有何不同。

sentences.en: Or, you know, let's open this up to genders rather than necessarily pigeonholing them.
sentences.zh: 或者，让我们把这个话题扩展到所有性别，而不是非要给它们贴上标签。

sentences.en: But your experience is that your sister has a diagnosis of autism.
sentences.zh: 但你的经历是你的妹妹被诊断出患有自闭症。

sentences.en: And so you've kind of learnt quite a lot about those differences, really, haven't you, Hannah?
sentences.zh: 所以你确实学到了很多关于这些差异的知识，对吧，汉娜？

sentences.en: Absolutely, yes.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: And it's very apparent that both within society and within the world of psychology, there is this stereotyping of what autism should look like.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，无论是在社会中还是在心理学界，对于自闭症应该是什么样子，都存在着刻板印象。

sentences.en: And it's based upon a lot of research with mostly male participants.
sentences.zh: 而且它是基于大量以男性为主要参与者的研究。

sentences.en: So there's been quite a huge lack of understanding of how autism actually presents in girls or people who are not male.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于自闭症在女孩或非男性群体中实际上是如何表现的，存在着巨大的认知缺失。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And a book that I was recently involved with called An Autistic Anthology is looking at mental health professionals who have an autism diagnosis or who understand themselves to fit within an autism framework.
sentences.zh: 我最近参与了一本书，叫《自闭症选集》（An Autistic Anthology），它关注的是那些患有自闭症或认为自己符合自闭症框架的心理健康专业人士。

sentences.en: And actually, I would say the majority of the people in that book are female, which I think it shows us that we're moving in a very, you know, neuro-informed direction.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我想说书中的大多数人都是女性，我认为这表明我们正在朝着非常了解神经多样性的方向发展。

sentences.en: Certainly very different than when I was an aspiring psychologist and, you know, I was doing some reading around the topic when I was a trainee.
sentences.zh: 这当然和我作为一名有抱负的心理学家时非常不同，当时我还是实习生，读了一些关于这个主题的资料。

sentences.en: And the book Aspergirls by Rudy Simone is a really, really interesting read.
sentences.zh: 鲁迪·西蒙（Rudy Simone）写的《Aspergirls》一书读起来真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: But, you know, being able to share that knowledge with parents in CAMS services was really powerful, actually, and really helped the validation.
sentences.zh: 但是，能够与CAMS（儿童和青少年心理健康服务）服务的家长分享这些知识，实际上非常有力量，也确实帮助了验证。

sentences.en: And, you know, to kind of, yeah, to know how to optimally support either yourself to thrive or someone in your family, in your work group, in your friendship circle.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，了解如何以最佳方式支持你自己茁壮成长，或者支持你的家人、工作组、朋友圈中的某个人。

sentences.en: It's a really, really important conversation to have, Hannah.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常、非常重要的对话，汉娜。

sentences.en: Absolutely, definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是，肯定的。

sentences.en: And I think some of the very real problems with that stereotyping is focused on those diagnostic probleMs.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种刻板印象带来的一些非常现实的问题集中在诊断难题上。

sentences.en: So there's a massive underdiagnosis where boys are currently four times more likely to receive a diagnosis than girls.
sentences.zh: 目前存在严重的诊断不足，男孩获得诊断的可能性是女孩的四倍。

sentences.en: And around 80% of autistic girls are first misdiagnosed with things such as anxiety or personality disorders, depression, ADHD,
sentences.zh: 大约80%的自闭症女孩最初被误诊为焦虑症、人格障碍、抑郁症、多动症等，

sentences.en: things that aren't quite exactly what they're struggling with.
sentences.zh: 这些并不是她们真正挣扎的问题。

sentences.en: So they don't receive that support in the correct time.
sentences.zh: 所以她们没有在正确的时间得到支持。

sentences.en: And that, of course, leads to late diagnosis, which is a huge problem because girls are getting diagnosed in their teens or even into adulthood, whereas boys are, on average,
sentences.zh: 当然，这导致了诊断延迟，这是一个巨大的问题，因为女孩通常在十几岁甚至成年后才被诊断出来，而男孩平均在五岁左右就被诊断出来了。

sentences.en: diagnosed around age five.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种刻板印象和知识匮乏确实产生了非常现实的影响，我们需要真正解决这个问题。

sentences.en: So there are very real impacts of that stereotyping and that lack of knowledge that we need to address, really.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 如果人们问，哦，为什么她们会得到其他诊断？

sentences.en: And if people are like, oh, you know, why would they be getting alternate diagnosis?
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，那些符合自闭症谱系诊断困难的人，确实可能在很多方面感到挣扎。

sentences.en: You know, just to speak to that point, really, it's that people who have difficulties that fit within an autism spectrum diagnosis really might struggle with a number of areas.
sentences.zh: 例如，她们更容易患上抑郁症、焦虑症，

sentences.en: For example, they're more likely to end up with depression, with anxiety,
sentences.zh: 有时比没有这些困难的人更容易饮酒过量。

sentences.en: more likely to kind of sometimes drink more alcohol units than someone who doesn't have those difficulties.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是多年来试图让自己适应那些并不一定适合你的环境所带来的后果。

sentences.en: And so it's those years of trying to fit yourself into environments that aren't necessarily helping to fit around you.
sentences.zh: 你不得不进行所有的修正和改善，这非常非常困难，也可能导致自闭症倦怠的症状。

sentences.en: You know, you're having to do all of that amending, all of that amelioration, which is very, very difficult and can lead to kind of symptoms of autistic burnout as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，这可能有助于人们理解为什么人们最终会得到其他诊断，而实际上，正如你所说，

sentences.en: So, you know, that might help people understand why people are ending up with other diagnoses when, in actual fact, like you say, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果她们能在那个框架和视角下被理解，并从很小的时候就得到帮助去了解自己，也许就像她们的男性同龄人一样，

sentences.en: if they've been understood within that framework, within that lens and helped to understand themselves from a much younger age, perhaps like their male counterparts,
sentences.zh: 那对她们来说将是一个多么大的机会啊。

sentences.en: just how much of an opportunity that would have been for them.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我认为谈论自闭症伪装（masking）非常重要，因为它在女孩中似乎更为普遍。

sentences.en: And I think it's very important to talk about autistic masking because it is seen to be more prevalent in girls.
sentences.zh: 所以我们思考一下，这些年轻女孩从社会中接收到了什么样的信息，以至于她们必须改变或隐藏自己的一部分，才能融入并被接受。

sentences.en: So we think about what messages are these young girls receiving from society that they have to change or hide parts of themselves in order to fit in and be accepted.
sentences.zh: 以及这对她们的心理健康所产生的影响。

sentences.en: And then the impacts that that's then having on their mental health as well.
sentences.zh: 因此，在没有被诊断的情况下，她们接收到的信息是：做自己是不对的。

sentences.en: So without being diagnosed, they're receiving this message that it's not OK to be who they are.
sentences.zh: 这其中伴随着太多的创伤。

sentences.en: And there's so much trauma associated with that.
sentences.zh: 所以我倾向于把伪装看作是一种创伤反应，因为她们是在回应那些关于她们是谁的非常负面的信息。

sentences.en: So I like to think of masking as a trauma response because they're responding to these very negative messages that they are receiving about who they are.
sentences.zh: 无论那是否正确。

sentences.en: Whether or not that's OK.
sentences.zh: 我认为作为一个社会，

sentences.en: And I think as a society,
sentences.zh: 我们真的需要努力克服这一点，因为这些孩子接收到关于她们应该或不应该是什么样子的信息，并且觉得她们不能做自己，这是不对的。

sentences.en: we really need to work to overcome this because it's not OK that these people are these children are receiving these messages around what they should or shouldn't be like and that they feel as though they can't just be who they are.
sentences.zh: 我可以凭经验说，当我妹妹被诊断出来后，她诊断前后的表现差异很大，因为她能够卸下伪装。

sentences.en: I can speak from experience that when my sister was diagnosed, the difference between her presentation before diagnosis compared to Aska after because she was able to unmask.
sentences.zh: 她简直像换了一个人，她说话的方式、语调、使用语言的方式，

sentences.en: Like she was almost a completely different person, the way that she spoke, her tone, the way that she used language,
sentences.zh: 她能够开始进行自我刺激（stimming），这些都是我们以前没见过的行为。

sentences.en: the fact that she was able to start stimming and these were behaviours that we hadn't seen before.
sentences.zh: 伪装会产生巨大的影响，它消耗了太多的精力和时间，确实会导致倦怠。

sentences.en: Masking can have such a huge impact and it takes up so much energy and so much time and it does lead to burnout.
sentences.zh: 然后你还要承受所有相关的创伤，这可能会导致情绪不稳定人格障碍等问题，这是一种创伤驱动的障碍。

sentences.en: And then you have all of the trauma associated with that, which then could lead to things like emotionally unstable personality disorder, which is a trauma driven disorder.
sentences.zh: 然后还有很多共病问题随之而来。

sentences.en: And then you have lots of comorbidities that come come into play.
sentences.zh: 关于伪装及其影响，以及我们作为一个社会向自闭症群体成员传递了什么信息，绝对有必要进行深入的探讨。

sentences.en: And it's there's a huge conversation definitely to be had around masking and the impacts of that and what messages are we as a society giving to members of the autistic community?
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我想我们可能应该说明一下，以防有人不确定，你妹妹已经允许我们谈论她了。

sentences.en: And I think it's probably worth us saying, in case anyone is unsure, your sister's given us permission to talk about her.
sentences.zh: 我们没有透露她的名字，没有使用她的照片，但我们是在谈论你作为她姐姐的经历，以及你如何帮助倡导，

sentences.en: We're not naming her, we're not using her photos, but we're talking about your experiences of of being her sister and kind of helping to advocate,
sentences.zh: 同时也帮助他人理解什么是自闭症以及它在女孩身上是如何表现的。

sentences.en: but also helping others to understand what autism is and how that looks in girls.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，也要谢谢你的妹妹。

sentences.en: So, yes, thank you to your sister as well.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 与自闭症的刻板印象相比，我在我妹妹身上看到的一些主要差异是过度顺从，

sentences.en: Some of the main differences that I see in my sister compared to what the stereotypical view of autism is would be over compliance,
sentences.zh: 被贴上安静、害羞和选择性缄默的标签，有大量的焦虑和伪装。

sentences.en: the being labelled as quiet, shy and selectively mute, having lots of anxiety and masking.
sentences.zh: 这些是我认为属于女性自闭症叙事的一部分的特征，它们往往被排除在关于自闭症应该是什么样子的主要讨论之外。

sentences.en: These are traits that I associate as being part of that female autism narrative, which are often left out of the primary conversation around what autism should look like.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些特征需要被更多地认识和讨论。

sentences.en: And these are traits that need to be recognised and spoke about more, I think.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以人们观看这个视频可能有各种各样的原因。

sentences.en: So people might be watching this video for all kinds of reasons, actually.
sentences.zh: 我们可能正在接触那些想知道自己是否能了解自己或寻求诊断的人。

sentences.en: We might be reaching people themselves that are wondering whether they might be able to understand themselves or pursue diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 我们可能正在接触那些开始对自己的孩子，或者有时是他们的兄弟姐妹，或者他们的父母产生疑问的家长，

sentences.en: We may be reaching parents of people who are starting to have questions around their children or maybe sometimes, you know,
sentences.zh: 有许多原因让人们在YouTube或MP3上偶然发现这一集。

sentences.en: their siblings or, you know, their parents, you know, there's many reasons why someone might have stumbled across this episode either on YouTube or as an MP3.
sentences.zh: 但如果有人，例如，了解他们的孩子是女性，并且他们正在尝试抚养她们，

sentences.en: But if someone, for example, understands their child to be female and they're trying to parent them,
sentences.zh: 但开始注意到也许在学校里，她们并没有像他们认为的那样茁壮成长。

sentences.en: but are starting to notice maybe in school they're not thriving in the way that they think they are capable of doing.
sentences.zh: 也许存在伪装行为。

sentences.en: Maybe there's masking going on.
sentences.zh: 也许当她们回到家时，因为精疲力竭，她们真的会产生强烈的情绪崩溃。

sentences.en: Maybe when they're getting home, they're really having kind of a strong emotional fallout kind of from exhaustion.
sentences.zh: 老师可能会看到什么？

sentences.en: What kind of things might teachers be seeing?
sentences.zh: 家长在另一端可能会看到什么？

sentences.en: What kind of things might parents be seeing at the other end?
sentences.zh: 汉娜，你能为我们详细讲讲吗？

sentences.en: Could you talk us through that a little bit, Hannah?
sentences.zh: 绝对可以。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 在学校期间，伪装是很典型的，她们可能想躲在教室后面。

sentences.en: So during school, it's quite typical to mask and they might then want to hide at the back of the class.
sentences.zh: 她们可能很安静。

sentences.en: They might be quite quiet.
sentences.zh: 老师典型的评价是她们很乖，但需要多发言。

sentences.en: The typical thing teachers would say is that they're a delight to teach, but they need to speak up more.
sentences.zh: 然后当她们回到家，一切都变了。

sentences.en: And then when they get home, all of that changes.
sentences.zh: 她们卸下了伪装。

sentences.en: They unmask.
sentences.zh: 也许她们在家里声音大了一些，家人无法理解为什么她们在学校里话那么少。

sentences.en: Maybe they're a bit louder at home and family members can't understand why then they're not speaking so much at school.
sentences.zh: 她们看起来非常失调和混乱。

sentences.en: And they seem so dysregulated and disrupted.
sentences.zh: 或者她们可能会退缩到房间里，产生相反的效果，几乎退缩到自己内心，保持安静，独自坐着，几乎是为了从她们那天为了表现正常而不得不经历的一切中恢复过来，

sentences.en: Or they might just retreat into the room and have the opposite effect where they almost retreat into themselves and they're just quiet and they can just sit with themselves and almost recover from everything that they've had to go through that day just to try and present normally,
sentences.zh: 而这甚至是不应该做的事情。

sentences.en: which is something that they shouldn't even have to do.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 通常当我们与家长，甚至与自闭症患者周围的成年人一起工作时，我们会想，实际上，

sentences.en: And often when we're working with parents or even adults who are around people with autism, it's thinking about, well, actually,
sentences.zh: 你创造了一个如此可爱的家庭环境，让她们能够真正做自己，并感到舒适地进行那种卸下伪装，并可能表现出她们的一些挫折感，这真的很棒。

sentences.en: it's really wonderful that you've created such a lovely home where they're able to really be themselves and to feel comfortable to kind of do that unmasking and to maybe show some of their frustrations.
sentences.zh: 也许她们整天都在压抑，但实际上一旦她们回到家，

sentences.en: Maybe they've been keeping a lid on it all day, but actually as soon as they get home,
sentences.zh: 她们的承受窗口就会缩小很多，以至于她们会变得更加敏感。

sentences.en: their kind of window of tolerance is that much more reduced that they're going to be more reactive.
sentences.zh: 我知道把这看作一种力量真的很棘手，因为家长会觉得，学校里的人得到了她们最好的一面，而我只得到了她们精疲力竭后的残余。

sentences.en: And I know that's really tricky to think about that as a strength because parents are like, well,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我想这是在赋予人们力量，让他们能够考虑在不同环境下保持更一致的自我，并思考这是否感觉良好。

sentences.en: all of their people at school are getting the best of them and I'm just getting the kind of burnt ends.
sentences.zh: 我们当然正在努力教育世界，这样做是可以的。

sentences.en: But actually, I guess it's empowering people to be able to perhaps think about being a more consistent self across the settings and whether that feels OK.
sentences.zh: 你知道，也许并不总是需要伪装。

sentences.en: And we're certainly trying to educate the world that that is OK.
sentences.zh: 绝对是，是的。

sentences.en: You know, maybe masking isn't needed all of the time.
sentences.zh: 当她们能够卸下伪装时，是她们感觉最舒服的时候。

sentences.en: Absolutely, yes.
sentences.zh: 所以她们能在家里这样做显然是一种力量。

sentences.en: When they're able to unmask, it's when they feel most comfortable.
sentences.zh: 这意味着她们感到舒适，而且家长创造了一个足够有同情心的环境，让她们觉得可以这样做。

sentences.en: So the fact that they can do that at home is obviously a strength.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对是一种力量。

sentences.en: It means that they're comfortable and the parents have created a compassionate enough environment that they feel able to do that.
sentences.zh: 唯一的缺点是她们无法在家庭之外或学校里这样做。

sentences.en: So it's definitely a strength.
sentences.zh: 而这更多地与社会看待自闭症的方式有关。

sentences.en: The only disadvantage then is the fact that they're not able to do that outside of the home or at school.
sentences.zh: 我觉得一旦人们有了诊断，对这些行为就会有更多的理解和同情，以某种方式行事也会更容易被接受。

sentences.en: And that's more to do with the way society perceives autism.
sentences.zh: 所以在诊断之前，伪装肯定会让人感觉更多。

sentences.en: I feel once people have the diagnosis, there's a lot more understanding and compassion towards these behaviours and it's a bit more acceptable to act in certain ways.
sentences.zh: 我想如果个人不明白自己为什么与众不同，她们会觉得需要做更多的事情来融入。

sentences.en: So prior to diagnosis, masking can definitely feel a lot more.
sentences.zh: 这会让人感到非常不知所措，而能够支持她们度过难关，并解开她们对自己的一些负面叙述，理解为什么这些叙述存在，

sentences.en: I guess the individual will feel that they need to do that more in order to fit in if they don't understand why they are different.
sentences.zh: 并不是她们的错，因为她们被告知不应该做自己。

sentences.en: And that can that can feel very overwhelming and just being there to support them through that and through unpicking some of these negative narratives that they have about themselves and understanding why those exiSt.
sentences.zh: 这绝对不是她们的错。

sentences.en: And it's not their fault that they're being told that they shouldn't be who they are.
sentences.zh: 并理解那不是我们要支持的叙事。

sentences.en: It's absolutely not their fault.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And understanding that that's not a narrative that we're going to support.
sentences.zh: 我可以问一下你妹妹被诊断时多大吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: Can I ask how old your sister was when she was diagnosed?
sentences.zh: 她当时13岁。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 所以她是晚诊断。

sentences.en: So she was 13.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，她被诊断为焦虑症和选择性缄默症。

sentences.en: So she was late diagnosed.
sentences.zh: 所以心理健康专业人士确实认识到出了问题，她有选择性缄默，她很焦虑，但他们没有转诊进行诊断。

sentences.en: And prior to that, she had been diagnosed with anxiety and selective mutism.
sentences.zh: 这些事情被错过并发生误诊是非常普遍的。

sentences.en: So the fact that mental health professionals were recognising something is wrong, she is selectively mute, she is anxious, but they're not referring her for a diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这让我很生气，

sentences.en: It's so common for these things to be missed and for misdiagnosis to occur.
sentences.zh: 心理健康专业人士没有认识到这些是女孩自闭症的症状，我们需要更早地转诊更多的女孩进行诊断，而不是等到她们精疲力竭或身体无法承受。

sentences.en: So it makes me quite angry, to be honest,
sentences.zh: 因为事情发展到我妹妹在学校里真的非常非常挣扎，必须采取一些措施。

sentences.en: that mental health professionals are not recognising that these are symptoms of autism in girls and that we need to be referring more girls for diagnosis sooner rather than waiting until they reach burnout or that they physically can't cope.
sentences.zh: 而这种晚诊断的影响意味着她无法转入特殊学校，因为她没有那个标签。

sentences.en: Because it got to the stage where my sister was really, really struggling in school and something really needed to be put in place.
sentences.zh: （注：此条原文缺失，根据上下文补全）

sentences.en: And the impacts of that late diagnosis meant that she was not able to transition to a specialist school because she did not have that label.
sentences.zh: （注：此条原文缺失，根据上下文补全）

sentences.en: Even though the mainstream environment was not appropriate for her, she was struggling and she wasn't able to keep up.
sentences.zh: 尽管主流环境并不适合她，但她一直在挣扎，却无法跟上进度。

sentences.en: And one of the things she developed was school avoidance because it's just such a traumatic environment to be in as a neurodiverse person.
sentences.zh: 她产生的问题之一就是逃学，因为对于神经多样性群体来说，那样的环境实在太具创伤性了。

sentences.en: So the fact that she was kind of forced into that environment because she was diagnosed with an inappropriate label,
sentences.zh: 所以，她因为被贴上了一个不恰当的标签，而被迫进入那种环境，

sentences.en: it just demonstrates why it's so important to recognise these things sooner rather than later.
sentences.zh: 这恰恰说明了为什么尽早识别这些问题是如此重要。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And when I was working in CAMHS, what you'd often see is, is things went really well in primary school.
sentences.zh: 当我在儿童及青少年心理健康服务中心（CAMHS）工作时，经常看到的情况是，孩子们在小学阶段表现得非常好。

sentences.en: But then when you get to moving into year seven, suddenly you've got to have more accountability.
sentences.zh: 但到了七年级，突然之间，你必须承担更多的责任。

sentences.en: You've got to kind of navigate yourself.
sentences.zh: 你必须学会如何自我引导。

sentences.en: The environments often tend to be a lot noisier.
sentences.zh: 环境往往变得嘈杂得多。

sentences.en: You're having to remember to take all of your different bits and pieces on different days.
sentences.zh: 你必须记得在不同的日子带上各种不同的零碎物品。

sentences.en: You're having to cope around sometimes much bigger, you know, taller people.
sentences.zh: 你还得学着去应对周围那些有时高大得多的人。

sentences.en: There's lots of jostling.
sentences.zh: 到处都是推推搡搡。

sentences.en: The corridors are really busy.
sentences.zh: 走廊里总是非常拥挤。

sentences.en: Sometimes it really starts to really starts to become apparent that actually the wheels almost begin to fall off at year seven and beyond.
sentences.zh: 有时，到了七年级及以后，情况真的开始变得显而易见，就像车轮开始脱落一样。

sentences.en: And that can be almost really difficult because the teachers perhaps have grown up with the child from being age four and have grown with them in perhaps in the same school and have really understood how to help get the best out of this out of this young person.
sentences.zh: 这可能非常困难，因为老师们可能从孩子四岁起就看着他们长大，在同一所学校里共同成长，真正了解如何帮助这个年轻人发挥出最好的水平。

sentences.en: And then, you know, they go to secondary school and you don't have any of that.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，他们上了中学，这些支持全都没有了。

sentences.en: You're starting from scratch and perhaps there's less consideration, there's less adjustment.
sentences.zh: 一切都要从头开始，而且可能缺乏关怀，缺乏调整。

sentences.en: You're having to just kind of run with, you know, what the generic provision is.
sentences.zh: 你只能被迫去适应那些通用的规定。

sentences.en: And before you know it, like it's a really difficult environment to be in.
sentences.zh: 还没等你反应过来，那已经变成了一个非常难以生存的环境。

sentences.en: And, you know, I'm again reflecting on my time working in CAMHS, but people would kind of start to, like you say, like to start to school avoid,
sentences.zh: 而且，我再次回想起在CAMHS工作的时光，人们会开始，就像你说的，开始逃学，

sentences.en: start to really struggle if they needed to go and speak to a teacher about something that would feel like a really, really impossible thing to do.
sentences.zh: 如果他们需要去和老师谈论某件事，那会让他们感到非常、非常不可能做到，从而开始真正挣扎。

sentences.en: And would be so practised and kind of made to be this really, really big thing that felt impossible.
sentences.zh: 这会被反复练习，被放大成一件感觉根本无法完成的大事。

sentences.en: It felt like trying to climb a mountain, you know, in just with the wrong equipment and sometimes ended in self-harm and ended in inpatient admission.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像是装备错误却要去攀登一座高山，有时最终导致了自残和住院治疗。

sentences.en: And at that point, we'd be like, oh, I wonder if actually you've ever considered whether, you know, your daughter or yourself, you know, might be autistic.
sentences.zh: 到了那个阶段，我们就会想，噢，不知道你是否考虑过，你的女儿或者你自己，可能患有自闭症。

sentences.en: And then the diagnosis might happen.
sentences.zh: 然后诊断可能才会发生。

sentences.en: But what are the opportunities if this happens, like you say, at such a younger age that we miss out all of that distress?
sentences.zh: 但如果这一切发生得更早，就像你说的，我们能避免所有这些痛苦，那该有多好？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And this is one of the reasons why the self-harm and suicide rates are so high for members of the autistic community.
sentences.zh: 这也是自闭症群体中自残和自杀率如此之高的原因之一。

sentences.en: One study that I came across suggested that people with autism were seven times more likely to die by suicide than the general population.
sentences.zh: 我读到过的一项研究表明，自闭症患者死于自杀的可能性是普通人群的七倍。

sentences.en: And that is a huge, huge difference.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大、巨大的差异。

sentences.en: It's so disheartening to realise what is happening to these people.
sentences.zh: 意识到这些人正在经历什么，真是令人沮丧。

sentences.en: And it's not their fault.
sentences.zh: 而且这并不是他们的错。

sentences.en: And it's something that shouldn't be happening.
sentences.zh: 这是不应该发生的事情。

sentences.en: Given the advancements that we've had in mental health research, this is something that really should have been tackled.
sentences.zh: 鉴于我们在心理健康研究方面取得的进展，这本应是早就该解决的问题。

sentences.en: This is something that mental health professionals should know about.
sentences.zh: 这是心理健康专业人员应该了解的事情。

sentences.en: And the fact that it's leading to things such as suicide and self-harm.
sentences.zh: 而且它正在导致自杀和自残等后果。

sentences.en: And these are children we're talking about as well, not just adults.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的不仅是成年人，还有孩子。

sentences.en: It's definitely something that we need to be talking more about and fostering more compassion towards.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是我们需要更多讨论并培养更多同理心的话题。

sentences.en: Yeah, it really matters and they're important conversations to have in every life, every person matters.
sentences.zh: 是的，这真的很重要，在每个人的生活中，这些都是重要的对话，每个人都很重要。

sentences.en: Can I ask how old your sister is currently?
sentences.zh: 我可以问一下你妹妹现在多大吗？

sentences.en: She's 17 now.
sentences.zh: 她现在17岁了。

sentences.en: So typically at age 17, someone would be in kind of sixth form.
sentences.zh: 通常在17岁时，一个人应该在读预科（Sixth Form）。

sentences.en: They've come out the other side of their GCSEs.
sentences.zh: 他们已经完成了GCSE考试。

sentences.en: Is that the case for your sister?
sentences.zh: 你妹妹是这种情况吗？

sentences.en: No, so as I mentioned previously, my sister was transitioned to a mainstream high school that she struggled with.
sentences.zh: 不是的，正如我之前提到的，我妹妹被转到了一所主流高中，但她在那儿适应得很艰难。

sentences.en: And then we managed to move her to specialist school once she had her diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 后来在她确诊后，我们设法把她转到了一所特殊学校。

sentences.en: But because of all the trauma she experienced through the mainstream school, she was still avoiding.
sentences.zh: 但由于她在主流学校经历的所有创伤，她仍然在逃避。

sentences.en: She was still unable to cope even in a specialist school.
sentences.zh: 即使在特殊学校，她也无法应对。

sentences.en: So she was transitioned then to homeschooling and she still finds even that, even being around one person who's unfamiliar in an environment that she's familiar with,
sentences.zh: 所以她后来转为在家教育，但即使是这样，即使是在她熟悉的环境中与一个不熟悉的人相处，

sentences.en: it's still very overwhelming for her.
sentences.zh: 对她来说仍然非常难以承受。

sentences.en: So she's being homeschooled, but she is not going for any exams at the moment because that would be, that would just be a bit much.
sentences.zh: 所以她现在在家接受教育，但目前没有参加任何考试，因为那对她来说负担太重了。

sentences.en: So we've delayed a year.
sentences.zh: 所以我们推迟了一年。

sentences.en: She would be taking her exams this summer.
sentences.zh: 她本该在今年夏天参加考试的。

sentences.en: So we've delayed that at the moment.
sentences.zh: 所以我们目前推迟了。

sentences.en: That's not something that we're considering because it's not something that's appropriate for her.
sentences.zh: 这不是我们考虑的事情，因为它对她来说并不合适。

sentences.en: But she is persisting with education in other ways.
sentences.zh: 但她正在以其他方式坚持学习。

sentences.en: So one of my sister's strengths is that she's amazing with animals and she really, really enjoys horse riding.
sentences.zh: 我妹妹的强项之一是她非常擅长与动物相处，而且她非常、非常喜欢骑马。

sentences.en: So she goes several times a week and she's learning also stable management.
sentences.zh: 所以她每周去几次，还在学习马厩管理。

sentences.en: So she's learning how to take care of horses, how to clean them, how to feed them.
sentences.zh: 她在学习如何照顾马匹，如何给它们清理，如何喂养它们。

sentences.en: And she's amazing.
sentences.zh: 她真的很棒。

sentences.en: She could look at a horse, tell you exactly what breed, the name of its coat and what food it needs to eat.
sentences.zh: 她看一眼马，就能告诉你确切的品种、毛色名称以及它需要吃什么食物。

sentences.en: Absolutely everything just by looking at it.
sentences.zh: 只要看一眼，什么都知道。

sentences.en: She's amazing with that.
sentences.zh: 她在这一方面非常出色。

sentences.en: So this is an alternative avenue that we're exploring that's much more appropriate for her.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们正在探索的一条替代途径，对她来说更合适。

sentences.en: And I think that's something that's important when you're educating people with autism, that the mainstream and the typical way of sitting exams might not actually be appropriate.
sentences.zh: 我认为在教育自闭症患者时，这一点很重要，即主流教育和那种典型的考试方式可能并不适合他们。

sentences.en: And that's OK.
sentences.zh: 那也没关系。

sentences.en: It's fine to find something that works for them because chances are that they might not actually be able to work in the traditional sense anyway,
sentences.zh: 找到适合他们的方法是很好的，因为他们很可能无法以传统方式工作，

sentences.en: because that in my sister's case anyway, that would be too overwhelming for her to cope with.
sentences.zh: 因为以我妹妹的情况来说，那对她来说太难以承受了。

sentences.en: So something where she can work with animals and her favourite being horses.
sentences.zh: 所以，从事与动物相关的工作，尤其是她最喜欢的马，就很适合。

sentences.en: And she loves also sheep, farm animals, really.
sentences.zh: 她也喜欢绵羊，其实就是农场动物。

sentences.en: That's being able to explore that in a much more flexible sense is amazing.
sentences.zh: 能够以一种更灵活的方式去探索这些，真是太棒了。

sentences.en: And it's great that after the almost traumatic journey that she's been through of education,
sentences.zh: 而且，在她经历了几乎是创伤性的教育历程之后，

sentences.en: that she's now at a stage where she can really focus on something she's interested in and she can just pursue that.
sentences.zh: 现在她能专注于自己感兴趣的事情并去追求它，这真是太好了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I love that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我喜欢这样。

sentences.en: That's so nice.
sentences.zh: 那太好了。

sentences.en: And actually, you know, there's there's lots of kind of literature and experiences and case studies about equine therapy and actually how helpful that can be.
sentences.zh: 其实，关于马术治疗及其有效性的文献、经验和案例研究有很多。

sentences.en: So maybe that's as part of her healing as part of what, you know, as well as part of what lights her up.
sentences.zh: 所以，也许这不仅是她疗愈的一部分，也是点亮她生活的一部分。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And to see the difference when she's on a horse.
sentences.zh: 看到她骑马时的变化真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: So my sister is selectively mute.
sentences.zh: 我妹妹有选择性缄默症。

sentences.en: So normally she won't talk if we're out in the community or around people she's not familiar with.
sentences.zh: 所以通常情况下，如果我们出门在外或者周围有她不熟悉的人，她是不会说话的。

sentences.en: She tries to sign, but sometimes signing can be overwhelming as well because she she doesn't like to feel observed.
sentences.zh: 她尝试用手语，但有时手语也会让她感到压力，因为她不喜欢被注视的感觉。

sentences.en: So that can be difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能很困难。

sentences.en: But when she's on a horse, she will go out on hacks and things and she will signal to traffic.
sentences.zh: 但当她骑在马上时，她会去野外骑行，还会向交通车辆打手势。

sentences.en: And that's absolutely amazing.
sentences.zh: 那真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: She's able to signal and to communicate to cars and people she doesn't know.
sentences.zh: 她能够向汽车和她不认识的人打手势并进行交流。

sentences.en: But if she's not on a horse, it's it's too much and it's not something she's able to do.
sentences.zh: 但如果她不在马上，那对她来说就太难了，她做不到。

sentences.en: But to see that difference and knowing that she has these skills, it's just what context is she able to use them in.
sentences.zh: 但看到这种差异，知道她拥有这些技能，关键在于她在什么情境下能够使用它们。

sentences.en: And it's it's absolutely amazing.
sentences.zh: 这真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Yeah, it really is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And I guess it's making her think about wanting to protect that horse and, you know, for that horse to be respected and given, you know, the the the room that it needs and,
sentences.zh: 我想这让她开始思考要保护那匹马，让它受到尊重，给它所需的空间，

sentences.en: you know, not have the traffic be too noisy or too faSt.
sentences.zh: 并且不让交通变得太吵或太快。

sentences.en: And it's really helping her to be assertive, you know, for herself, but for the horse as well.
sentences.zh: 这真的在帮助她变得自信，不仅是为了她自己，也是为了那匹马。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And that's that's something I think the impact of animals for people with autism as a therapeutic thing is absolutely amazing.
sentences.zh: 我认为动物对自闭症患者的治疗作用影响是绝对惊人的。

sentences.en: And it's definitely a strength.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是一个优势。

sentences.en: And if you are supporting someone with autism, thinking about whether it's appropriate, some something that they can do and engage in with animals might be beneficial to them.
sentences.zh: 如果你正在支持自闭症患者，考虑一下他们是否可以参与与动物相关的活动，这对他们可能是有益的。

sentences.en: Yeah, we haven't got time for it today, but we are going to get together for a future episode thinking about the theoretical kind of frameworks for for autism.
sentences.zh: 是的，今天我们没时间细谈，但在未来的节目中，我们会聚在一起探讨自闭症的理论框架。

sentences.en: Could you briefly just tell us what those are that people might hear about?
sentences.zh: 你能简要告诉我们人们可能会听到哪些框架吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: So if you're working in an LD service or if you're working with people with autism, you might hear a lot about positive behavior support.
sentences.zh: 如果你在学习障碍服务部门工作，或者与自闭症患者一起工作，你可能会经常听到“积极行为支持”（PBS）。

sentences.en: And this is looking at the meaning behind mostly challenging behaviors.
sentences.zh: 这主要是为了探究挑战性行为背后的含义。

sentences.en: So why do they occur?
sentences.zh: 它们为什么会发生？

sentences.en: What are they trying to communicate?
sentences.zh: 他们试图传达什么？

sentences.en: Because often it is a method of communication.
sentences.zh: 因为这通常是一种沟通方式。

sentences.en: And how then do we support them to get what they need without the need to be challenging or to self harm?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们如何支持他们获得所需的东西，而无需采取挑战性行为或自残？

sentences.en: And it contrasts directly with applied behavior analysis, which is almost the opposite.
sentences.zh: 这与“应用行为分析”（ABA）形成了直接对比，后者几乎是相反的。

sentences.en: It looks at trying to use positive reinforcement and punishment methods to reduce challenging behaviors.
sentences.zh: 它试图使用正向强化和惩罚方法来减少挑战性行为。

sentences.en: And it's completely ignorant of what the meanings could be.
sentences.zh: 它完全忽略了这些行为可能代表的含义。

sentences.en: So PBS was developed from ABA to kind of overcome some of these issues.
sentences.zh: 所以PBS是在ABA的基础上发展起来的，旨在克服其中的一些问题。

sentences.en: And it's a much more compassionate view.
sentences.zh: 它是一种更具同理心的观点。

sentences.en: It's normally used in combination with trauma informed care, which is very, very important when working with neurodiverse people,
sentences.zh: 它通常与“创伤知情护理”结合使用，这在与神经多样性群体工作时非常、非常重要，

sentences.en: because it helps you to look at all of the trauma associated with going through a world that's not designed for you and all of the problems that you will face because of that.
sentences.zh: 因为它能帮助你审视一个人在不为他们设计的世界中生活所带来的所有创伤，以及他们因此面临的所有问题。

sentences.en: And it's very, very important to keep these things in mind when working or talking with someone who is neurodiverse.
sentences.zh: 在与神经多样性人士工作或交谈时，牢记这些是非常、非常重要的。

sentences.en: So that's kind of the brief overview that I can give on what those techniques are.
sentences.zh: 这就是我能给出的关于这些技术的简要概述。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Yeah, it does.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And we will come back to it in future.
sentences.zh: 我们以后会再回过头来讨论这个话题。

sentences.en: But, you know, you are clearly so knowledgeable.
sentences.zh: 但是，你显然知识非常渊博。

sentences.en: You've clearly spent a lot of time learning about these things so that you can optimally help your sister,
sentences.zh: 你显然花了很多时间学习这些知识，以便能最好地帮助你的妹妹，

sentences.en: but probably optimally help your clients in services that you're working with as well.
sentences.zh: 同时也可能最好地帮助你在工作中服务的客户。

sentences.en: Which area, which population are you working with as an AP currently?
sentences.zh: 你目前作为助理心理学家（AP）在哪个领域、服务哪个人群？

sentences.en: So I'm working two part time AP roles.
sentences.zh: 我目前担任两份兼职的助理心理学家工作。

sentences.en: So I work within CAMHS with children.
sentences.zh: 我在CAMHS为儿童服务。

sentences.en: And then I also work within an adult LD service.
sentences.zh: 同时我也在成人学习障碍服务部门工作。

sentences.en: Within that role, I go to social care homes and I help support both clients and staff who might be experiencing issues with,
sentences.zh: 在那个岗位上，我会去社会护理院，帮助支持那些可能在如何支持学习障碍或自闭症患者方面遇到问题的客户和员工，并努力培养那种富有同理心的方法，

sentences.en: how do you support someone with a learning disability or with autism and trying to foster that compassionate approach
sentences.zh: 并解决社会护理系统内的一些系统性问题。

sentences.en: and work through some of those more systemic problems within the social care system.
sentences.zh: 我们该如何在那种环境中支持这些人？

sentences.en: And how do we support those people within that kind of environment?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想他们绝对找对了人来做这份工作。

sentences.en: Well, I'd say they've definitely got the right person for that job.
sentences.zh: 你听起来让人感觉非常可靠，

sentences.en: You know, you sound, you know, you feel like a really safe pair of hands really,
sentences.zh: 而且，你还拥有一颗善良、富有同理心的心，你会希望这样的人去照顾你关心的人。

sentences.en: but also, you know, nice, compassionate hands that you'd want someone to be working with someone that you care about as well.
sentences.zh: 所以，做得好。

sentences.en: So well done to you.
sentences.zh: 我希望，无论你现在还是将来申请博士学位，都能获得丰硕且应得的成功。

sentences.en: I hope that, you know, whether it's your time to apply to doctorates now or in the future, that you have really rich, well-deserved success there.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 我认为培养同理心非常重要，不仅是对自闭症群体，而是对每个人。

sentences.en: I think it's so important to foster compassion, not just towards the autistic community, but towards everyone.
sentences.zh: 人与人之间有很多差异，但重要的是要保持同理心。

sentences.en: There's so many differences between people, but it's important to just be compassionate.
sentences.zh: 这就是心理学的目标，去关怀他人。

sentences.en: And that's what psychology aims to do, to care for others.
sentences.zh: 如果不是想帮助别人，我想你也不会进入这个领域。

sentences.en: And I don't think you'd be in this field if you didn't want to help people.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽可能从那种富有同理心的角度去看待问题，这就是我在做每件事时真正努力去做的。

sentences.en: So looking as much as you can from that compassionate point of view, that's what I really try to do with everything.
sentences.zh: 如果我能给你的听众留下一条信息，那就是尽量保持尽可能多的同理心。

sentences.en: And if that's, if there's one message that I can leave your listeners with, it would just be to try and be as compassionate as possible.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我为有志于成为心理学家的人开设的新网站将在本期节目发布时上线。

sentences.en: And my new website for aspiring psychologists will have launched by the time this episode goes out.
sentences.zh: 但是，在我的“关于我”部分，我想它表达了同理心是多么重要。

sentences.en: But, you know, in my about me section, I think it is, it's kind of saying actually how important compassion is.
sentences.zh: 即使你从不买书，从不听我的播客，也请务必拥抱同理心，拥抱以同理心为中心的疗法，无论是对自己还是对你身边的人，因为这真的会改变生活。

sentences.en: And even if you never buy a book, if you never listen to a podcast episode by me, please, please embrace, embrace, you know,
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: compassion and compassion focused therapy and for yourself and those that you're with, because it is life changing.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间，Hannah，也感谢你向我提议这期节目。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目还不错。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for your time, Hannah, and for pitching this episode to me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你的时间，Hannah，也感谢你向我提议这期节目。

sentences.en: Hope it's been okay.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目还不错。

sentences.en: We will get a date booked in for that next episode.
sentences.zh: 我们下一集会把日期定下来的。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: It's been a really, really invigorating, useful conversation.
sentences.zh: 这是一次非常、非常有启发性且有益的谈话。

sentences.en: That's great.
sentences.zh: 那太棒了。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: Oh, you're so welcome.
sentences.zh: 哦，不用客气。

sentences.en: Thank you for coming.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你来参加。

sentences.en: Oh, thank you so much for our guest today, Hannah.
sentences.zh: 哦，非常感谢我们今天的嘉宾汉娜。

sentences.en: Hannah.
sentences.zh: 汉娜。

sentences.en: She just blew me away with her insight, her passion, her preparedness, you know.
sentences.zh: 她的洞察力、热情和准备工作真的让我印象深刻，你知道的。

sentences.en: What a great episode.
sentences.zh: 真是精彩的一集。

sentences.en: What a great gueSt.
sentences.zh: 真是位出色的嘉宾。

sentences.en: So thank you, Hannah.
sentences.zh: 所以，谢谢你，汉娜。

sentences.en: And I am hopeful for you for whatever your career brings next.
sentences.zh: 我也祝愿你未来的职业生涯一切顺利。

sentences.en: Would you like to pitch me an episode for the Aspiring Psychologist podcast?
sentences.zh: 你想为《有抱负的心理学家》播客提议一期节目吗？

sentences.en: Please do come and connect with me on socials.
sentences.zh: 请一定要在社交媒体上与我联系。

sentences.en: That's the easiest place to pitch me your episodes.
sentences.zh: 那是向我提议节目最简单的方式。

sentences.en: Hannah pitched me via LinkedIn.
sentences.zh: 汉娜就是通过领英向我提议的。

sentences.en: Why don't you do the same?
sentences.zh: 你为什么不也这样做呢？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我在所有平台上的名字都是玛丽安·特伦特博士。

sentences.en: If you're looking for some inspiration on how to reflect, perhaps how to see yourself as an autistic mental health professional, please do check out An Autistic Anthology,
sentences.zh: 如果你正在寻找关于如何反思的灵感，或者如何看待自己作为一名自闭症心理健康专业人士，请务必看看《自闭症选集》这本书，

sentences.en: which is a book that was published in November 2024.
sentences.zh: 这是一本于2024年11月出版的书。

sentences.en: Or, of course, for more general experiences of clinical psychology, check out the Aspiring Psychologist Collective and the Clinical Psychologist Collective too.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果想了解更多关于临床心理学的普遍经验，也可以看看《有抱负的心理学家合集》和《临床心理学家合集》。

sentences.en: If it's your time and you're ready for the next step and you want some guidance for your career around research, around cognitive behavioural therapy, around reflective practice,
sentences.zh: 如果时机已到，你准备好迈出下一步，并且想要在研究、认知行为疗法、反思实践方面获得职业指导，

sentences.en: around confidence, you know, taking that imposter syndrome and, you know, making it be banished.
sentences.zh: 或者关于自信，你知道的，克服冒名顶替综合症，让它彻底消失。

sentences.en: To help you to confidently take control of your career, do check out the Aspiring Psychologist membership, which you can join from just £30 a month with no minimum term.
sentences.zh: 为了帮助你自信地掌控自己的职业生涯，请务必查看“有抱负的心理学家”会员计划，每月仅需30英镑起，且无最低期限要求。

sentences.en: But if you did want to join for a longer term, there are incentives around which get you one-to-one time with me for free.
sentences.zh: 但如果你想加入更长的时间，还有一些激励措施，可以让你免费获得与我一对一的时间。

sentences.en: What's not to like there?
sentences.zh: 这有什么不好呢？

sentences.en: Please do come along to my website where you can access my free psychology success guide.
sentences.zh: 请务必访问我的网站，在那里你可以获取我免费的心理学成功指南。

sentences.en: My brand new website is www.aspiring-psychologiSt.co.uk.
sentences.zh: 我的全新网站是 www.aspiring-psychologist.co.uk。

sentences.en: That is hot off the press.
sentences.zh: 这可是新鲜出炉的。

sentences.en: I only met with my website editor today to get that signed off.
sentences.zh: 我今天才刚和网站编辑确认并签署了最终版本。

sentences.en: So you might already have seen that on my social media, but this is the first time I've been able to mention it in my podcast recording.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能已经在我的社交媒体上看到了，但这还是我第一次在播客录音中提到它。

sentences.en: So please do come along.
sentences.zh: 所以请一定要来看看。

sentences.en: Come and check it out.
sentences.zh: 快来看看吧。

sentences.en: Let me know what you think to it.
sentences.zh: 让我知道你的想法。

sentences.en: I would love your feedback.
sentences.zh: 我很期待你的反馈。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for being part of my world.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你成为我世界的一部分。

sentences.en: Come and join the free Facebook group,
sentences.zh: 快来加入免费的Facebook群组，

sentences.en: The Aspiring Psychologist Community with Dr. Marianne Trent.
sentences.zh: “有抱负的心理学家社区”，由玛丽安·特伦特博士创建。

sentences.en: If you're looking to become a psychologist,
sentences.zh: 如果你想成为一名心理学家，

sentences.en: then let this be your guide.
sentences.zh: 那就让这成为你的指南吧。

sentences.zh: 有这个播客在身边，你离获得资格就不远了。

sentences.zh: 这就是玛丽安·特伦特博士的《有抱负的心理学家》播客。

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能赚到除了出卖时间换取金钱之外的收入，会怎样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士，自2019年以来，我一直在开发被动和经常性收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有个激动人心的消息。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's one-to-many program is now open for enrollment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特的“一对多”项目现在开放报名了。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员计划和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022, and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己曾在2022年完成了这个项目，此后也支持了两批心理学家走过他们的旅程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses, plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的推荐链接加入，你将获得苏菲的奖励，以及我独家提供的额外支持包，无需额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四次小组大师班、大师课程、个性化指导、一份福特纳姆和梅森的礼品，以及限时的一对一辅导奖励。

sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我都在这里。
